Source: [GitHub issue 1485](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1485).

The report links the public pm-web capacity harness and unbraind/pm-web issue 211. It separates three untraced and three traced runs, pre-append delay, index-lock wait lower bound, downstream SDK classification, polling and SSE delivery. The proposed investigation must retain those distinctions and must not infer universal starvation from one perturbed run. This PR records intake only; implementation remains unclaimed.
GH-1485: Bound history-index reader contention before authoritative appends

Evaluate and bound writer delay from exclusive history-event-index readers while preserving authoritative history, invalidation, fallback and late-fact visibility. The reported mixed reader/writer workload retained correctness but breached its 2000ms real-time delivery SLO in one traced run.

Reproduce with isolated traced and untraced cohorts and report writer lock wait separately from downstream detection; Choose and document a bounded snapshot/fair-lock/critical-section protocol from measured attribution; Preserve authoritative fallback, committed invalidation and late-fact visibility; Prove zero lost or duplicate events, zero history drift and the declared end-to-end latency budget under mixed SDK and CLI writers.
Measure reader-versus-writer lock attribution and implement a bounded history-index read/write protocol without losing committed facts.
UI and agent watchers can observe project context without delaying authoritative mutations beyond a measured collaboration budget.
GH-1485 reports a 2247.5ms pre-append delay with at least 2071.0ms waiting for the history-index lock under 100 readers and ten writer lanes.
History-index reads preserve committed-fact correctness while writer delay and end-to-end delivery remain within an explicit, reproducible collaboration budget.

Intake only: GH-1485 reports one breached traced run among three, 50 updates and 5000 receipts delivered exactly once, on a shared four-CPU host. The attribution includes scheduling/open/retry overhead and has not been reproduced here. No fix or performance acceptance is claimed.

value.text: Negative control: both new snapshot tests fail against the unchanged baseline: an index query refuses while the writer file lock is held, and a reader suspended inside stream stat blocks an authoritative append beyond 1500ms. Candidate snapshot queries and recency reads acquire no writer locks, close SQLite before filesystem validation, and retain stream-size plus invalidation checks. First focused run passes all 49 tests. The distinct optional-rebuild availability escape is tracked as pm-xj80p9 and claimed for this same delivery.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Protocol choice: capture rows and size receipts in one synchronous SQLite read transaction, then close it before filesystem validation. Check stream sizes, pending/committed invalidations and projection file generation without acquiring writer locks. Concurrent generation changes and native SQLite BUSY/LOCKED conditions use authoritative fallback directly; only missing or damaged caches request one optional zero-retry rebuild. This keeps correctness authentication while removing both long validation critical sections and repair storms.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Optimistic cache validation needs a distinct transient result. Treating every refused snapshot as cache damage can recreate writer contention through optional rebuilds even after ordinary reads release all writer locks.

Read projection rows and size receipts in one SQLite transaction, close before asynchronous validation, and verify generation/invalidation state without writer locks. Transient reads use authority directly; optional writes never wait for native SQLite contention.
Implemented nonblocking history snapshots and bounded native SQLite contention with authority-preserving recovery.
